the SASB interpersonal process variables of "helping" and "blaming" were significantly related to outcome in the third therapy session.
(1) the SASB model is a useful tool for the study of psychotherapeutic process, and (2) the interpersonal process variables that were studied differentiated between the high- and low-change cases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the structural model of interpersonal relations, the structural analysis of social behavior (SASB), to the study of differential psychotherapeutic process and outcome.
the development and application of an interpersonal theory and methodology that can be used in the study of interpersonal processes and their relation to outcome in psychotherapy.
the development of a new method for analyzing interpersonal processes in psychotherapy.

SASB has been found to be an extremely useful tool in the study of interpersonal processes in psychotherapy.
SASB is a valuable tool for the investigation of interpersonal process in psychotherapy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the therapist's behavior in a session is a better predictor of outcome than is the patient's behavior in the session.
the more the therapist helps, affirms, and understands the patient, the better the patient's outcome.
the interpersonal process of therapy is more important in predicting differential outcome than the personality characteristics of either the patient or the therapist.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to understand how the therapist's and patient's behavior is influencing each other in order to understand how therapy works.
we need to be more aware of how we use our language and our words.
SASB is an excellent tool for studying social behavior and its impact on psychotherapy outcomes.
